title: The Roman sanctuary at Cova Dones
dek: More than a hundred inscriptions entered the record before the goddess, the word MALACI, and the sanctuary’s social world had settled into an agreed interpretation.
whyTracked: The site has a stable identity, active conservation and epigraphic work, and central questions likely to sharpen through formal publication.

current.assessment: The inscriptions and archaeological context are documented, but the deity, MALACI, chronology, relationship to water, and interpretation of women’s participation remain preliminary.
current.nextReviewTrigger: Review for a peer-reviewed paper, epigraphic catalog, revised readings, material analysis, or a new identification of the sanctuary or deity.

openQuestions: Which deity or deities were worshipped in the chamber?
Will artifact and inscription analysis substantiate the proposed role of women and water?

watchFor.trigger: The research team publishes inscriptions, readings, dating, or material analysis.

watchFor.description: Revised identification of the sanctuary or deity
watchFor.trigger: New evidence changes the Domina or MALACI interpretation.

observations.headline: Point-zero observation
observations.summary: Researchers documented at least 120 Latin inscriptions in Cova Dones and proposed that part of the cave served as an organized Roman-period sanctuary involving women.

sources.title: 120 Roman inscriptions discovered at Cova Dones

observations.headline: Admitted to The Wake pilot
observations.summary: Admitted because the first report preserves unusually consequential unknowns that later epigraphy and material analysis may resolve.
